Notation (from the surrounding pages): [x^k] = prod_{n>=1}(1-x^{kn}) = (x^k;x^k)_inf. Gauss's formula 6 is the Jacobi triple product: prod(1+x^{2n-1}y)(1+x^{2n-1}/y) * [xx] = sum_n x^{n^2} y^n. Write phi(q) = 1+2q+2q^4+2q^9+... Then phi(-q) = [q]^2/[q^2] and phi(q) = [q^2]^5/([q]^2[q^4]^2). The page continues the previous one, which expressed phi(-x), phi(-x^3), phi(-x^9) as (x^3;x^6) times x^{-1/8} times a lacunary series of the form sum c_m x^{m^2/8} over odd m.

[37] (28) minus (30). By [28], phi(-x^9)/(x^3;x^6) = sum over m prime to 6 of x^{(m^2-1)/8}. By [30], phi(-x^3)/(x^3;x^6) = [x^3] = sum chi_12(m) x^{(m^2-1)/8} (Euler's pentagonal theorem with x -> x^3). Subtracting leaves the m with chi_12(m) = -1, i.e. m ≡ ±5 mod 12:
phi(-x^9) - phi(-x^3) = 2(x^3;x^6) x^{-1/8}(x^{25/8}+x^{49/8}+x^{289/8}+x^{361/8}+...) = 2(x^3;x^6)(x^3+x^6+x^36+x^45+x^105+x^120+...).

Triple product with x -> x^6, y -> x^5 y:
prod(1+x^{12n-1}y)(1+x^{12n-11}/y) [x^12] = sum x^{6n^2+5n} y^n = 1 + x/y + x^11 y + x^14/y^2 + x^34 y^2 + ...

[38] Same with x -> x^3, y = 1 (my step): x^3 [x^36] prod(1+x^{36n-3})(1+x^{36n-33}) = x^3 sum x^{18n^2+15n} = x^3+x^6+x^36+x^45+... Hence
phi(-x^9) - phi(-x^3) = 2x^3 [x^36](-x^3;x^36)(-x^33;x^36)(x^3;x^6).

[39] phi(-x^3) - phi(-x) = 2x [x^12](-x;x^12)(-x^11;x^12)(x;x^2), i.e. the case y = 1 of the displayed formula, times (x;x^2).

[40], [41] are [38], [39] with x -> -x, after multiplying by -1:
phi(x^3) - phi(x^9) = 2x^3[x^36](x^3;x^36)(x^33;x^36)(-x^3;x^6)
phi(x) - phi(x^3) = 2x[x^12](x;x^12)(x^11;x^12)(-x;x^2).

[42] (30) minus (29):
phi(-x^3) - phi(-x) = 2(x^3;x^6) x^{-1/8}(x^{9/8}-x^{25/8}-x^{49/8}+x^{81/8}+x^{225/8}-...).
The series is +x^{m^2/8} for odd multiples of 3 and -x^{m^2/8} for m ≡ ±5 mod 12. Gauss remarks that comparing with [39] factorizes this series.

[43] [34] times [39]. [34] is phi(-x)+phi(-x^3) = 2[x^12](x;x^2)(-x^5;x^12)(-x^7;x^12). The product is
phi(-x^3)^2 - phi(-x)^2 = 4x[x^12]^2 (x;x^2)^2 (-x;x^2)/(-x^3;x^6).
Using (x;x^2) = [x]/[xx], (-x;x^2) = [xx]^2/([x][x^4]) and (-x^3;x^6) = [x^6]^2/([x^3][x^12]):
= 4x [x][x^3][x^12]^3/([x^4][x^6]^2).

[44] [36] times [41], analogously:
phi(x^3)^2 - phi(x)^2 = -4x[x^12]^2 (-x;x^2)^2 (x;x^2)/(x^3;x^6) = -4x [xx]^3[x^6][x^12]^2/([x][x^3][x^4]^2).

[45] Quotient [43]/[44]:
= -(x;x^2)(x^3;x^6)/((-x;x^2)(-x^3;x^6)) = -[x]^2[x^3]^2[x^4][x^12]/([xx]^3[x^6]^3).

[45b] Product [43]*[44]:
= -16x^2 [xx]^3[x^12]^5/([x^4]^3[x^6]).

Purpose: a systematic table of level-12 (cubic) theta identities. Sums, differences, products and quotients of phi(±x) and phi(±x^3) are written as infinite products / eta-quotients. This is evidently preparation for degree-3 transformation (modular equation) work; the next page does the same with the complex combinations phi(-x^3) ± i phi(-x).
errors: [44]: phi(x^3)-phi(x) = -[41], so the right side of [44] needs a minus sign (leading term is -4x). The manuscript shows a blotted or overwritten sign at the start of [44], and the minus is correctly carried into [45] and [45b] (-16xx). So this is at most a corrected slip, not an error in the results.

[45], middle expression: the correct infinite product is prod_{n odd}((1-x^n)/(1+x^n)) times prod_{n odd, 3|n}((1-x^n)/(1+x^n)). That means exponent 1 for odd n prime to 3 and exponent 2 for odd multiples of 3. The transcription gives exponents 3 (for n = 1, 5, 7) and 1 (for n = 3, 9); that is either a misreading or a slip by Gauss. The final eta-quotient -[x]^2[x^3]^2[x^4][x^12]/([xx]^3[x^6]^3) is correct and corresponds to exponents 1/2.
[45b]: the left side is written in abbreviated form {(1-2x^3)^2-(1-2x)^2}{...}, meaning the full theta series. The result is correct.
[42]: the series is only partly written ('+x^{225/8} - &c'). The terms shown are correct; m = 11, 13 correctly drop out.

results.modern_name: theta-function identity of level 36 / cubic modular identity via Jacobi triple product
results.usually_credited_to: Ramanujan-type identities (Ramanujan's notebooks, ch. 19-20; Berndt); triple product: Jacobi 1829, known to Gauss

results.what: phi(-x^3)-phi(-x) = 2x(x;x^2) f(x,x^11) with f(x,x^11) = (x^12;x^12)(-x;x^12)(-x^11;x^12); equivalently phi(q)-phi(q^3) = 2q chi(q) f(-q,-q^11)
results.usually_credited_to: Ramanujan (notebooks; cf. Berndt, Ramanujan's Notebooks III)

results.modern_name: weight-1 level-12 eta-quotient identities for differences of squares of theta functions (related to cubic theta functions/ sums of two squares with x^2+3y^2)
results.usually_credited_to: Ramanujan; Borweins' cubic theory (1991) for related forms

results.what: Quotient and product of the two differences of squares as single eta-quotients ([45], [45b])

deep.surprise_reason: Gauss's Nachlass is known (Werke III, VIII, X) to contain the triple product and many theta-product identities from c. 1800-1810. Systematic level-3 and level-12 identities of this Ramanujan type are a notable but not unexpected detail. I am unsure whether these specific formulas appear in the published Werke.
